method: Shooting ratio is the total recorded footage divided by the finished runtime, so 10:1 means ten hours were shot for each finished hour. Durations are read as bare seconds, mm:ss or h:mm:ss with the minutes and seconds fields under 60, and are converted to whole seconds. Runtime may be 1 second to 100 hours and footage 1 second to 10,000 hours; footage shorter than the runtime is refused because the cut cannot be longer than the material it came from. The reverse calculation multiplies the runtime by a target ratio from 1 to 1000 with at most two decimals and rounds the required footage to the nearest second. Unused footage is the footage minus the runtime and the usable share is the runtime divided by the footage, expressed as a percentage. The model is an accounting identity, not a measurement: it assumes every second of the cut comes from the footage counted and that all recorded material is available, so it says nothing about camera cards, storage, takes, coverage or what a particular production should shoot. Text, negative values, exponent notation and extra clock fields are refused with the field named. Nothing is stored, uploaded or transmitted.
